content.thinking:
I'm framing the symptom as "account pages failed for many shoppers" and tracing the causal chain, starting with how error rates spiked from baseline to peak during the incident, drawing on the relevant metrics and citations.

Next I dig into the direct cause: requests hit a ZeroDivisionError in the spend summary code starting at 23:09. That traces back to the monthly-spend-feature flag flipping on, which activated the dividing code path — I'm ruling out deploys as a cause since none occurred, and confirming the flag was previously off with the service healthy. Beyond that, the evidence doesn't explain why the code path actually divides by zero, so I'm stopping the causal chain there since there's no further data to support it.

The onset timing lines up with when the flag switch happened at 23:09. For contributing factors, I'm noting the flag rolled out to all traffic at once with no staged rollout or automatic halt mechanism when errors rose — a gradual rollout could have caught this earlier. I'm also flagging that there's no evidence the code path behind the flag was tested or reviewed before being switched on, since it fails specifically on account pages.

As for whether paging mattered, someone did manually revert the flag around 23:16:32, roughly a minute after the alert fired, so it's unclear a formal page would have sped up the response — I'm inclined to skip this as a contributing factor.

I also want to flag that the division-by-zero bug at spend_summary.py:47 was never actually fixed, just worked around by disabling the flag, so re-enabling monthly-spend-feature would likely cause the same account page failures again.

Now I'm drafting concrete action items: fix the root-cause division bug, add a test covering the zero-divisor case with the flag on, roll out flag changes gradually to limit blast radius, auto-revert flags when error rates spike, and route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to actual on-call paging.

I'm also noting a process item — keep monthly-spend-feature disabled until the fix ships — and moving into lessons learned, crediting Argus for correctly identifying the flag change as the likely cause shortly after the alert fired, citing the division-by-zero log lines, while distinguishing that the manual rollback was done by a person rather than Argus itself.

On the went_wrong side, nobody paged despite this being a candidate flag for it, and there's a discrepancy worth flagging: the flag provider only recorded one change in the hour before 23:16:38 (the on-switch at 23:09), yet the person claims they manually rolled it back around 23:16:32 — meaning that rollback doesn't appear in the provider's history at that timestamp.

For assumptions, I'm noting that the customer loss estimate comes from comparing against earlier weeks, and the root cause is inferred from correlating the flag switch timing with errors starting the same minute, with the human-reported rollback not independently confirmed by Argus. The plain-language cause is that enabling the new monthly-spend feature triggered the code causing the issue.

Now I'm drafting the root cause statement pinpointing the ZeroDivisionError in the spend summary code at a specific file and line, noting the record doesn't explain why the divisor was zero, then starting the chain of impact beginning with the rise in server error rates on account page requests.

I'm tracing the error logs showing the ZeroDivisionError first appeared during a specific time window, then connecting it back to the monthly-spend-feature flag being switched on by an admin, with flag evaluations shifting from off to mostly on then fully on within that minute. I'm also ruling out a recent deploy or rollout change as the cause, since no deployments occurred the day before and all replicas were confirmed running the same revision.

I'm being careful to stop at what the evidence actually shows -- the record doesn't explain why that code path divides by zero, so I'll note that gap in the root cause rather than speculating further. Now I'm making sure the write-up avoids vague quantifiers and keeps specific references like the file path and line number intact.

action_items.item: Fix the spend-summary code at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 so that a zero divisor no longer fails the account page request.
Keep monthly-spend-feature off until the fix for the division by zero has shipped.
Add a test that renders the account page with monthly-spend-feature on, including the case where the divisor at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 is zero.
Roll out flag changes on io-shop to a small share of traffic first, and widen them only once the error rate holds steady.
Switch a flag on io-shop back off automatically when the share of server errors rises right after it changes.
Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to the on-call paging rotation.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed. The share of requests answered with a server error rose from {series_before} before the onset to {series_while_broken} on average while it was broken, and peaked at {series_at_worst}. The service's own log reported account page error rates of up to {Gbac1.5}, highest at {Gbac1.7}.

The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. This was logged {G5309.1} times over {G5309.3}, starting in the minute of the onset. Before that, only the usual client-disconnect errors were logged and account pages rendered normally.

ruled_out.what: A deploy or release of io-shop. The search for production changes in the day before the onset returned only the flag change, and no deploys came back.

causal_chain.step: That code path ran because admin switched on the feature flag monthly-spend-feature at {P1.1}. Every flag evaluation came back off before the switch. In the minute of the switch, {G971b.2} of {G971b.3} evaluations came back on, and every minute after that they all came back on. The division-by-zero errors began in that same minute.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Turning on a new monthly-spending feature also turned on code that tried to divide by zero while building customers' account pages, so those pages failed.

contributing_factors.factor: No staged rollout of the flag and no automatic halt on rising errors was seen. Most flag evaluations came back on within the minute it was switched, and all of them from the next minute.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Only a small share of account page requests would have hit the failing code before the rise in errors stopped the rollout, so fewer shoppers would have seen failures and for less time.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No test or check of the account page with monthly-spend-feature switched on was seen before the flag was turned on in production.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 could have been caught before the flag reached shoppers.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: An on-call responder would have been pulled in as soon as the alert fired, rather than the response depending on someone happening to notice.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

went_well: The Investigator named the monthly-spend-feature flag change as the likely cause {T13.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised, tying it to the division-by-zero log lines that began in the same minute.
The Intent Agent classified the person's message in the thread as a resolution {XW2.1 - XW1.1} after it was posted.

input.root_cause: Switching on monthly-spend-feature sent account page requests down the spend-summary code path, which raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, so those requests fail. The record does not show why the divisor there is zero.
input.still_at_risk: The code behind monthly-spend-feature that divides by zero was still in place, so switching the flag on again would fail account pages the same way.
input.symptom: Shoppers' account pages failed for many requests
